Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Planned: Model-serving continuity validation window & staggered driver consolidation (Jul 27-28)

Hi Sofia and AtlasHealth platform team,

Quick heads-up from Redwood Inference — we're scheduling a targeted validation window to run a staggered host driver consolidation and continuity drill in the US-East region on Jul 27-28 (two-night rolling window). This is a risk-reduction exercise: we will validate a consolidated driver/kernel combination across tenants and run failover drills to verify model-serving continuity and KV-cache warmup strategies.

Summary of what to expect:
- Window: Tue July 27 23:00 UTC → Wed July 28 07:00 UTC (per-host, staggered to avoid mass evictions)
- Impact: short (sub-60s) transient request throttling during host handoff for a small subset of capacity; no batch eviction for pinned Dedicated pools unless opted-in
- Safeguards: automatic fallback to compatible driver variant, KV-cache restoration protocol, and pre-run synthetic traffic to validate latency SLOs

Why we're doing it: we found subtle variance in a newer driver build that can trigger slow cold-starts for long-context requests. This validation reduces regression risk for model-serving at 99th percentile latencies.

What we need from you (AtlasHealth):
1) Confirm whether any workloads are explicitly pinned to host pools in us-east that should be excluded.
2) Flag any scheduled heavy inference jobs on Jul 27-28 so we can avoid overlapping experimental windows.

Attachments: driver_compat_matrix_v2.csv (compatibility matrix by instance type), runbook-model-serving-continuity.pdf (ops steps and rollback checklist).

If you'd like, we can run a short pre-window validation with your production-safe test key to show baseline vs validation behavior.

Thanks — Grace
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
[g] +1 415-555-0123
redwood.com

Note: internal ops plan and canary schedule: Jordan will run the canary at 23:10 UTC and report. Vivek owns rollback thresholds. Marissa will monitor KV warmup metrics. Neha will coordinate customer communications.

Hi Sofia — thanks for the quick reply and the ETL window note, that's helpful. A few clarifications from the ops side: 

- Synthetic traffic will be clearly labeled with X-Redwood-Test: true and a distinct User-Agent so your monitoring can filter it out. We'll also post a short webhook event to the URL you provide 5 minutes before each canary.
- Estimated latency delta during the canary (based on recent tests): typical P95 bump of ~80-120ms for long-context (>2048 tokens) requests while KV-cache is restoring on a newly consolidated host. P99 impact is expected to be under 250ms and short-lived. We'll abort if we see error rate >0.5% sustained for more than 2 minutes.
- Scheduling: we can avoid host actions between 00:30 and 02:00 UTC on Jul 28 per your request. Our staggered plan pushes the canary for that cluster to 22:40 UTC on Jul 27 and next host at 02:10 UTC — outside your ETL window.

Operational runbook highlights (from runbook-model-serving-continuity.pdf):
1) Pre-check: validate healthy KV-cache hitrate > 98% on target serving nodes.
2) Canary: run synthetic at 1 RPS per canary host for 3 minutes, compare P50/P95/P99 against baseline.
3) Rollforward: if canary passes, proceed to next staggered host; if fails, automatic fallback to prior driver variant + full KV-cache warmup.
4) Post-run: automated postmortem report generated and shared to the incident folder.

I'll post the exact webhook URL to you by EOD so you can whitelist it.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
